title: 6-Year-Old Chinese Girl Sets Rubik's Speed Record
paragraphs: A six-year-old girl from China has set a new women's world record for solving a Rubik's Cube.

Lian Yunzhi set the record for the fastest women's average time for solving the standard 3x3x3 cube. Her average time was just 4.27 seconds per cube. According to the World Cube Association, which organizes official speedcubing competitions, she is now the record holder.

Earlier in September, Lian first broke the record at an official competition in Wuhan, a city in central China, with an average of 4.52 seconds. One of her single solves there took only about 3.54 seconds. She then improved her own record to 4.27 seconds at another competition in Guangzhou, in southern China. According to China's state broadcaster CCTV, she is the only female speedcuber to have an average time of less than 4.5 seconds.

Lian's progress has been remarkable. She first tried to solve a Rubik's Cube when she was four years old, and at that time it took her 90 seconds. Since then, she has learned more than 1,300 formulas, which are sets of moves used to solve the cube. Recently, she has been practicing for two to three hours every day, and her parents have taken her to Shanghai to train with top coaches.
At first, Lian was not confident enough to take part in competitions. But as her results improved and she received more attention, she became more enthusiastic and trained harder.
Her mother, Lin Yangxi, said Lian used to be an introverted child, but now she is very confident wherever she goes.
